subject: Operator subprocess chain evidence for EU-only processing
messages:
From: Pierre Durand <pierre.durand@pharmalink.eu>
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal-ops@pharmalink.eu
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Operator subprocess chain evidence for EU-only processing

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this. As part of PharmaLink's EU-only processing acceptance, our privacy team needs a clear mapping of Redwood's operator/subprocessor chain and supporting evidence that processing for our tenant will be performed exclusively in the EU under the SCCs. Specifically we need:

- A list of all subprocessors involved in the inference data path (inference, KV cache, backups, monitoring, logging) and their jurisdiction.
- Evidence that data plane resources for our tenant will remain in the EU (region and availability zone info).
- SCCs execution confirmation and the last signed date.
- KMS key custody and location (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed) and whether any key material leaves the EU.
- Backup/restore retention and escape procedures for egress or operator access.
- Proof of deletion timeline (how quickly caches and backups are purged after deletion request).

I've attached our standard questionnaire (pharmalink_questionnaire_v2.pdf) — please populate sections 3, 4, and 7 and return. We have a compliance gate scheduled for next Wednesday; can we get an initial bundle before then?

Thanks,

Pierre Durand
Head of Privacy & Compliance
PharmaLink EU

Attachment: pharmalink_questionnaire_v2.pdf

Subject: Re: Operator subprocess chain evidence for EU-only processing (internal)

Ben / Jordan — attaching the operator matrix and SCCs mapping. I redacted internal ticket IDs that shouldn't be shared externally; the matrix contains subprocessors, function, region, contract status, and whether they have EU-only deployment options. Key points to surface to PharmaLink:

- Data plane (inference and KV caches) can be pinned to EU regions (we commonly use eu-central-1 and eu-west-2 depending on capacity).
- Backups are geo-redundant by default; for EU-only customers we can scope backups to EU regions and provide a retention window.
- SCCs were executed with PharmaLink's signature on 2027-09-01; master execution copy is sccs_mapping.pdf.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys in the customer's EU KMS (recommended). If using Redwood-managed keys, key material remains in EU HSMs for EU-only deployments.
- Deletion: KV cache purge within minutes for active caches; snapshot/backups deletion can take up to 30 days depending on scheduled backup cycles — we document and certify purge windows in the bundle.

I propose a short call with Pierre to walk the bundle Friday 17 Nov at 14:00 CET (I'll send calendar invite). If PharmaLink requires proof artifacts (audit logs, signed token of deletion), note that will require a scoped evidence request to ops and may take 48 hours to assemble.

Attachments: operator_access_matrix.xlsx, sccs_mapping.pdf

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Head, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Pierre — thanks for your patience. Apologies for the slight delay assembling items in one place. Attached is the consolidated evidence bundle we discussed: operator_access_matrix.xlsx (subprocessor list + jurisdictions), sccs_mapping.pdf (signed SCCs and execution note), and a populated version of your questionnaire (sections 3, 4, 7 completed). For convenience we've also dropped the artifacts into a shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-operator-evidence

High-level summary for PharmaLink compliance:
- EU-only data plane: For your tenant we will pin inference and KV cache workloads to EU regions (eu-central-1 primary).
- KMS custody: We recommend customer-managed KMS in the EU. If you opt for Redwood-managed keys, we confirm HSMs and key material do not leave EU boundaries for EU-only tenants.
- SCCs: Executed and countersigned (see sccs_mapping.pdf, signed 2027-09-01).
- Backups & deletion: Backups can be scoped to EU; standard snapshot retention for scoped deployments is configurable — we propose a 30-day backup retention with a documented purge process. Cache purge occurs within minutes; full snapshot wipe may take up to 30 days depending on backup cycles.
- Operator access: Limited to named operator roles, time-bound elevated access, and recorded in audit logs. We can produce an operator-access audit extract on request (48–72 hours to pull and sanitize).

Next steps: please confirm if the attached bundle is sufficient for the compliance gate. If you want the operator-audit extract or a short walkthrough call, we can schedule it this week — propose Thursday 22 Nov 10:00 CET or Friday 23 Nov 09:00 CET.
